rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Vegetation is the plant cover of a place, set by temperature, rain, soil and height. Nepal's cover changes quickly because the land rises from the Terai to the high Himalaya.
Below about 1000 m the belt is tropical. Sal, Shorea robusta, dominates, with sisau along rivers. This is the Terai and the inner Terai.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: From about 2000 to 3000 m the belt is temperate. Oak and Rhododendron arboreum, the national flower, are the markers. Rhododendron here is a flowering plant.  ·  Toward 4000 m, fir, birch and juniper thin out. The timberline is the last trees. Above it, alpine herbs and grasses continue until the snowline, which is higher.  ·  Forest and other wooded land cover about 45 percent of Nepal. The east is wetter than the west at the same height, so the species lists differ. Community forestry is a management success in the middle hills, not itself a belt.
